attempts.reason: The run had zero RPC/nonce/network errors and shared head/state root, but it is not green. Validator-2 still retained mahi_pre_admitted_pool.items=72 after an extra 30s settle, and validator-4's three ingress endpoints all collapsed even though they were driven from three different runner hosts.

runner_observations: The new dedicated runner root@203.0.113.19 was reachable and idle before the run: hostname ubuntu-24gb-nbg1-1, 12 vCPU, about 22 GiB available RAM, uptime about 10 minutes.
The weak validator-4 endpoints were not co-located on one runner. validator-4-p8645 ran on root@203.0.113.13, validator-4-p8646 on root@203.0.113.19, and validator-4-p8647 on root@203.0.113.10.

Runner profiles captured active kombat_loadgen processes on those three hosts during the load window: validator-4-p8645 around 51-65% CPU on root@203.0.113.13, validator-4-p8646 around 17-43% CPU on root@203.0.113.19, and validator-4-p8647 around 19-39% CPU on root@203.0.113.10.
Validator-2's endpoints were healthy by throughput at about 3162.4-3254.4 RPS, yet validator-2 still retained 72 Mahi pre-admitted items after an extra 30s settle.
conclusion: This is binned. The first four-runner rung did not recover a better green floor; it introduced a validator-4-side collapse across three different runners and preserved a validator-2 drain defect. The current green TPS remains item274's 42,221.2 committed TPS. The next move is validator-side investigation on validator-4 and the validator-2 residual tail, not a higher offered-load rung.
